approachQuestion.prompt: A display description is CHAR(c), JOIN(a,b), or REPEAT(k,a). Its text is respectively one character, concatenation of the child texts, or k copies of a's text. Return the zero-based p-th character of its text. Example: JOIN(CHAR(z),REPEAT(3,JOIN(CHAR(a),CHAR(b)))) describes zababab, so p=4 returns b.
constraints: The description is a read-only tree with n nodes, 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000, height h ≤ 1000, and no shared nodes.
1 ≤ k ≤ 1000000000. Every described length fits a signed 64-bit integer; 0 ≤ p < the total described length.
Length arithmetic, multiplication, remainder and indexing fixed-width integers take constant time. Let L denote total described length; it can be enormous.

options.text: At REPEAT(k,a), return the result for p divided by k within a.
options.feedback: REPEAT(3,JOIN(CHAR(a),CHAR(b))) at p=1 should return b; division by 3 selects a.

options.text: At every JOIN, select the left child whenever p is less than the number of description nodes in its left subtree.
options.feedback: A REPEAT subtree can have few nodes but describe many characters; node counts are not character offsets.

options.text: Compute and store the length of every description node once. To locate p, select the proper JOIN child using its left length, or replace p by p modulo the repeated child length at REPEAT; continue to a CHAR.
options.feedback: Lengths skip entire represented regions and repetition copies without producing their characters.

options.text: Compute lengths once, then build the full described text and index it.
options.feedback: A legal description can represent a billion characters with only a few nodes; expansion does work unrelated to the small query.

feedback.reason: Stored lengths count represented characters, not description nodes.
details: First recursively compute a length for each node into a node-indexed array: one for CHAR, the child-length sum for JOIN, and k times child length for REPEAT. Then descend from the root with p, subtracting the left length when taking a right JOIN child and taking remainder by child length at REPEAT. Return the reached CHAR.

Stored lengths count represented characters, not description nodes. At REPEAT, modulo child length selects the position within one copy; division by repetition count does not. JOIN subtracts the left length only on a right descent.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n be description node count and h its height. Count the newly allocated length array and recursive preprocessing frames; exclude input and returned character. Fixed-width arithmetic is constant time. No text expansion, copying, or hashing occurs. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: Length preprocessing costs n; the later single descent adds at most tree depth.
details: Computing all n lengths costs linear time and storage. The subsequent descent visits at most h+1 nodes; h is at most n, so it does not change either overall bound.
“O(L) time, O(L) auxiliary space”: The analyzed method stores lengths, not the expanded text.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: The query descent is depth bounded, but first computing and storing all node lengths costs work and space across the full description.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The newly computed length array and active preprocessing calls are auxiliary storage.
